scope: All 127 original headings reviewed; additional walkthroughs and planning references added.
method: Mechanics are paraphrased from linked sources. Editorial tips are recommendations and calculations, not developer promises or guaranteed outcomes. Wiki pages may be incomplete; named faction availability is not verified by a generic mechanics source.

sections.title: Welcome
facts: Torn permits one account per person; ownership and account-sharing restrictions matter from the start.
tips: Give each login a quick checklist: bars, education, job, cash, then whatever chaos Torn has planned for you.
Pick one goal before opening your wallet. Level 15, bigger stats and a healthy cash reserve all want a slice of it.

sections.title: Donator Status
facts: Using a Donator Pack grants 31 donator days and 60 points; subscriptions are a different product.
tips: Check today's pack price against the benefits you'll actually use. A shiny package isn't automatically a bargain.
If the in-game price fits your budget, that's an option too. Yesterday's price quote belongs in yesterday.

sections.title: Need Help? stuck somewhere?
facts: Official rules and help channels take precedence over player-written shortcuts.
tips: Tell people your goal, level, exact error and what you've tried. Help me help you beats it broke by a mile.
Crop out keys, passwords, email addresses and session tokens before sharing screenshots. Those are not show-and-tell material.

sections.title: Go further
facts: Education unlocks lasting perks; gym progression rewards consistent training.
tips: Keep a tiny mistake log and one next step per guide. Future you deserves better than another expensive rerun.
Give your plan a weekly check-up. You don't need six side hustles and a spreadsheet-induced headache on day two.

introduction.summary: Welcome to Torn. Let's protect the account, tame the bars and give your wallet a fighting chance.
corrections: Do not confuse subscription rewards with using a tradable Donator Pack.
checklist: Read the rules and secure the account. Boring now beats painful later.
Pick one goal and a budget that leaves an emergency cushion.
On a normal login, check bars, education and whether your cash is sitting somewhere sensible.

extras.title: Account and API-key hygiene
facts: Torn restricts software to authorised API data or the page a player manually loaded and is actively viewing.
tips: Give each trusted tool its own key with only the access it needs. One broken connection shouldn't take the whole circus down.
Never paste your Torn password, browser cookies or someone else's credentials into a helper. A helper doesn't need your house keys.

sections.title: Sidebar Top
facts: The sidebar groups account actions, game areas and player lists.
tips: Hover over the status before buying a cure. Diagnose first, throw money at it second.
Build a short route through your usual pages. Clicking every menu isn't a secret progression strategy.

sections.title: Icons
facts: Status icons distinguish ongoing effects and cooldowns.
tips: Read the timer, not just the pretty icon. A cooldown doesn't end because you looked at it intensely.
If an icon looks mysterious, inspect it in Torn before acting on an old screenshot. Tiny pictures can cause surprisingly large bills.

sections.title: Money
facts: Cash on hand is the exposure relevant to mugging; total net worth is a different measure.
tips: Know where the money is going before a sale lands. Your wallet is not a long-term storage facility with excellent security.
Keep a working float, then check how quickly you can access the rest. Rich on paper and broke at checkout is an awkward combo.

sections.title: Level
facts: Experience is hidden; winning and leaving a higher-level opponent is a documented levelling route.
tips: A big level number doesn't mean an easy fight. Your attack results are a better judge than your optimism.
If level 15 is the mission, take the upgrade when it's available. Don't accidentally become a committed level-holder.

sections.title: Points
facts: Points buy unlocks and refills; they cannot be placed in an ordinary direct trade.
tips: Split permanent unlocks from regular refills in your budget. Future you would like to afford both.
Check how much a refill will actually give you before buying it. Paying to top up an already-full bar is impressively unhelpful.

sections.title: Merits
facts: Upgrade tiers become more expensive: a ten-tier merit line costs 55 merits in total.
tips: Spend merits for the game you're playing now. Education reductions can be useful early on; they aren't a compulsory personality trait.
Check reset prices and free resets before experimenting. A casual click can become a very uncool invoice.

sections.title: Energy
facts: Normal regeneration is 5 energy per 15 minutes to 100; donator regeneration is 5 per 10 minutes to 150.
tips: Try to log in before your bar caps when life allows it. Full bars don't earn overtime.
Compare useful progress per energy: training, attacks or paid work. The biggest cash number isn't always the best deal.

sections.title: Nerve
facts: Nerve regenerates by one every five minutes; bonuses can make the displayed maximum differ from natural nerve.
tips: Watch crime skill separately from your nerve bar. They're related to crime, not identical twins.
Use natural nerve before buying more, and count materials and failed attempts. Gross income loves leaving those bits out.

sections.title: Happiness
facts: Above-maximum happiness resets at quarter-hour boundaries; it affects gym gains and Crimes 2.0 progression.
tips: Have the energy and supplies ready before boosting happy. Shopping during the countdown is a bold way to waste money.
Price a happy jump for your own stats first. Someone else's expensive ritual isn't automatically your best gym plan.

sections.title: Life
facts: Life normally regenerates by 5% of maximum every five minutes; full life alone does not remove hospital time.
tips: Check life, hospital status and medical cooldown separately. The game has several ways to say not yet.
Sort compatible meds before an attack session. Emergency shopping is rarely your most elegant financial moment.

sections.title: Chain
facts: A chain starts with ten successful attacks in five minutes, then needs a successful hit before its timer expires.
tips: Have backup hitters ready. One failed fight shouldn't turn the chain chat into a fire drill.
Follow the bonus-hit plan. Racing your own teammate for a milestone is teamwork's slightly embarrassing cousin.

sections.title: Mail Events & Awards
facts: Awards may change with crime-system migration; the wiki flags some requirements as incomplete.
tips: Check your current awards screen before funding a merit hunt. An old wiki requirement can send you on a very expensive detour.
Read faction mail and payment events before clearing them. The answer to where did my money go might already be sitting there.

sections.title: Areas
facts: The sidebar links to the main activity areas; access can depend on your current game state.
tips: If a page won't cooperate, check travel, jail and hospital status first. Sometimes you're not bugged; you're just unavailable.
Learn the useful city links. A stranger's mystery short URL is not a navigation upgrade.

sections.title: Home
facts: Torn's Home page supports rearranging and minimising information boxes.
tips: Put bars, education, perks and the stuff you actually use near the top. Your dashboard doesn't need to be a junk drawer.
Check important changes in game. A dated helper snapshot is a photograph, not a live CCTV feed.

sections.title: Items / Inventory
facts: Items include equipment, tools, materials and consumables, with different uses and trading restrictions.
tips: Check filters, equipment and anything committed elsewhere before declaring an item missing. Inventory hide-and-seek happens.
Read the effect and current price before using, binning or bulk-selling something unfamiliar. Mystery buttons can be pricey.

sections.title: City
facts: The city map supports item finds and faction-territory information.
tips: Collect your finds, then check what the unusual ones are worth. Found on the floor doesn't mean worth floor prices.
Learn the page you need instead of clicking like a caffeinated woodpecker. More clicks aren't a universal money printer.

sections.title: Job
facts: Starter jobs award daily pay, work stats and job points; explicitly passive specials can remain after leaving.
tips: Plan promotions around the required work stats. Today's tiny pay cheque isn't the whole story.
Compare lasting unlocks with company pay, trains and attendance rules. Pick the package, not just the loudest recruitment pitch.

sections.title: Gym
facts: Gyms have different training multipliers and unlock through gym experience plus membership purchases.
tips: Peek at the next gym's multipliers before paying. A new membership should do more than decorate your profile.
Record your actual gains. Your own before-and-after numbers beat a stranger's one-size-fits-everybody stat target.

sections.title: Properties
facts: Rent is prepaid; tenants can incur staff upkeep, and a rented property's vault is inaccessible.
tips: Add staff costs to the rent. Fancy housing is less fun when the employees discover invoicing.
Check the upgrades and lease length before paying for a travel setup. A lovely view won't hire the pilot for you.

sections.title: Education
facts: Courses can have prerequisites and drug-related expulsion can force a restart.
tips: Pick your next course before the current one ends and set a reminder. The admissions office doesn't chase you.
Know which perk or unlock you're working towards, and keep an eye on addiction. Restarting a course is not bonus studying.

sections.title: Crimes
facts: Crimes 2.0 has hidden crime experience and separate, visible skill for each crime.
tips: Use the Crimes 2.0 notes here, not an old Crimes 1.0 nerve ladder. Wrong rulebook, wrong party.
Choose cash, skill or unique outcomes as your goal. Trying to optimise everything at once usually just optimises confusion.

sections.title: Missions
facts: Contract standing changes with success, failure and declining; accepting every contract is not always beneficial.
tips: Read every condition before accepting: target, weapon and finish all matter. Duke is not grading your enthusiasm.
Price the supplies and energy, then leave time for an unavailable target. A deadline doesn't care that you were nearly ready.

sections.title: Newspaper
facts: The newspaper includes articles, job listings, property markets and bounties.
tips: Check the publication date. An ancient announcement wearing a fresh browser tab is still ancient.
Follow the actual article or announcement when chat repeats a claim. Torn's rumour department works very hard.

sections.title: Jail
facts: Busting success depends on several factors, and repeated attempts close together can reduce success rates.
tips: Compare waiting, bail and asking for a bust before burning more nerve. Panic-clicking isn't a legal defence.
Use the time where you can, but don't deliberately fail crimes for gym access. That's a creative route to a worse day.

sections.title: Hospital
facts: Hospital time and medical cooldown govern different restrictions; several exit methods have exceptions.
tips: Check the cooldown cost before grabbing the strongest med. Bigger is not always smarter.
Before paying for a revive, check your settings and agree whether payment needs success. Avoid bonus arguments after the hospital visit.

sections.title: Casino
facts: Casino tokens and casino-job points are different resources.
tips: Keep casino play inside a firm entertainment budget. Rent and training money should have other plans.
Don't raise stakes to recover losses. If it stops being enjoyable, take a break or use in-game self-exclusion.

sections.title: Hall Of Fame
facts: Some rankings show your position without exposing other players' private battle-stat identities.
tips: Watch your own progress over time. Comparing your first week with a veteran is a very efficient way to feel unnecessarily terrible.
Don't guess exact private stats from a rank, title or level. A leaderboard is not an X-ray machine.

sections.title: Factions / My Faction
facts: Faction membership provides shared resources, upgrades and coordinated activities.
tips: Compare duties and payout rules alongside perks. Great benefits can come with a surprisingly energetic calendar.
Ask when vault withdrawals are handled before parking your money there. Officers need sleep too.

sections.title: To join or not to join a faction
facts: New members normally begin with a 72-hour Recruit period and limited access.
tips: Ask what works immediately and what waits for full membership. The welcome mat and the benefits desk aren't always the same thing.
Pick attendance rules that fit real life. Your actual job probably won't accept faction chain as an absence note.

sections.title: Organized Crimes
facts: OCs 2.0 have planning and execution stages with role-specific requirements.
tips: Ask which role fits your chance and bring the required equipment. Arriving empty-handed is a memorable introduction.
Check readiness before flying or disappearing for a weekend. Sort replacements before the group starts asking where you went.

sections.title: Recruit Citizens
facts: Referral rewards are tied to genuine referred players' progression.
tips: Invite people who actually want to play and help them get started. A friend is more useful than an abandoned referral number.
Never make another account for referral rewards. One account per person is a rule, not a puzzle.

sections.title: Calendar
facts: Events may use player-selected time slots; dates in old guides are not an authoritative schedule.
tips: Save both dates and times from your own calendar. Starts Friday is not a complete battle plan.
Check what triggers the bonus: departure, use, claim or something else. Timing is where the small print earns its keep.

sections.title: Community Events
facts: Community competitions and seasonal systems have their own participation rules.
tips: Read eligibility, deadlines and delivery terms before sending anything. Entering first and reading later is the spicy option.
Keep the announcement and your receipt. A promised prize is easier to discuss when everyone can see the same agreement.

sections.title: Lists
facts: Friends, enemies and targets serve different organisational purposes.
tips: Use short, consistent notes. Future you should recognise a player without solving a miniature detective case.
Update the note when things change. Easy target from six months ago might now be a rather unpleasant surprise.

sections.title: Friends List
facts: Friends can have custom descriptions and status filters.
tips: Save good traders, mentors and service providers with a useful note. Nice person is pleasant but not very searchable.
Keep payment terms in a real conversation. A friend label isn't an insurance policy.

sections.title: Enemies List
facts: Enemies-list settings can block listed players from purchases across several markets.
tips: Check purchase-block settings before using this as a bookmark list. Accidentally banning your own customers is an unusual sales tactic.
Keep the notes factual and current. An old argument doesn't need to become a permanent checkout problem.

sections.title: Chats
facts: Public, group and private channels have different access and conduct rules.
tips: Pick the right channel for the message. The whole city doesn't need your shopping list.
Keep credentials out of every chat, even if someone claims to be support. Especially then.

sections.title: Chats Settings Panel
facts: Channel access depends partly on membership and game state.
tips: Tame notifications before a time-sensitive activity. Your phone doesn't need to impersonate a slot machine.
If a channel vanishes, check membership and game state first. It may be a status change, not a conspiracy.

sections.title: New Player Chat
facts: Access ends at level 13 or after 336 hours of accumulated play time.
tips: Ask the basic questions while you've got access. Everyone started somewhere, usually with several misunderstandings.
Once access ends, find a help forum or faction mentor. Don't make another account to sneak back into class.

sections.title: Global
facts: Global is for social discussion; trade advertising is not permitted there.
tips: Put sales adverts in the proper trade space. Global is not your personal billboard.
If nobody replies, improve the context instead of repeating yourself. Volume is not a substitute for clarity.

sections.title: Trade Chat
facts: Trade chat is for adverts; the documented limits are one message per 60 seconds and 125 characters.
tips: Make the advert useful: item, price basis and how to contact you. You're selling supplies, not writing a suspense novel.
Check today's channel rules before posting. Old advice to spam adverts has aged about as well as warm milk.

sections.title: Faction
facts: Faction chat is tied to membership.
tips: Check current orders with the organiser. A pinned message from the previous war may have retired without telling you.
Keep important supply and payout terms somewhere durable too. A busy chat scroll is a terrible filing cabinet.

sections.title: Company
facts: Company chat provides a shared channel for that company's members.
tips: Use the channel to coordinate trains, supplies and absences. Directors also appreciate fewer surprise plot twists.
Confirm informal promises against the company's actual policy. A chat shrug is not a clear contract.

sections.title: Hospital / Jail / Travel
facts: These channels appear and disappear with the relevant game state.
tips: Say where you are and what you need when asking for help. Please revive me is missing a few useful details.
Check the provider's Torn ID and agree the price before paying. Names and avatars can look suspiciously similar.

sections.title: Misc
facts: Torn Time follows UTC rather than a daylight-saving local timezone.
tips: Give deadlines a date and timezone. Tonight becomes a philosophical problem when your teammates live everywhere.
Keep an emergency float and useful supplies before a long activity. Prepared is cheaper than desperate.

sections.title: Time - TCT
facts: TCT is UTC year-round; India Standard Time is UTC plus 5 hours 30 minutes.
tips: For a handy example, 12:00 TCT is 17:30 IST. Near midnight, check which day you've landed on too.
Use a timezone-aware calendar for the team. Mental time arithmetic gets less charming during a countdown.

sections.title: NPC Looting
facts: NPC loot uses a contribution-based lottery; joining a fight does not guarantee an item.
tips: Check loot level and the attack plan before spending energy. Turning up is not the same as securing a prize.
Compare the cost with training or levelling first. An exciting lottery is still a lottery.

basic-elements.summary: All those buttons, bars and tiny icons explained. No advanced degree in staring at the sidebar required.
corrections: Happy helps Crimes 2.0 skill/experience gains; this is not the same as improving success chance.
Old city-find and chat assumptions should be checked against the current systems.
checklist: Check the timer before buying a cure or booster.
Keep training and education pointed at something you actually want to unlock.
If helper data looks old, confirm it in Torn before making an expensive decision.

extras.title: A resource check before expensive actions
facts: Energy, nerve, happy and their cooldowns do not all refill or reset in the same way.
tips: Check amount, cap, timer and your next action before using expensive supplies. Make the plan before pressing the shiny button.
After acting elsewhere in Torn, confirm important values in game. Your helper cannot read your mind or your other tab.

sections.title: The Magic Number
facts: Level 15 unlocks overseas travel; visible level and combat strength are not interchangeable.
tips: Chase reliable wins, not the biggest level number on the list. Confidence doesn't come with free medical supplies.
At 15, rethink training and income. You unlocked travel, not a lifelong contract to punch the same people.

sections.title: Levelling Targets
facts: Leaving after a win yields more level experience than mugging or hospitalising the same target.
tips: Build a little shortlist from fights you can actually win. Your own results deserve a vote.
Check the target's current status before spending energy. Old stats and inactivity aren't a warranty.

sections.title: Initial Preparation
facts: Equipment includes melee, firearms, temporary items and armour; damage and accuracy matter alongside item names.
tips: Equip what you bought and check ammo if you're using a gun. Your inventory isn't fighting on your behalf.
Borrow faction gear or price a modest upgrade before buying something glamorous. Looking expensive is not a battle stat.

sections.title: The Housing Situation
facts: A lease fixes its agreed terms; staff still create upkeep costs.
tips: Choose rent you can afford for the whole stay. Day-one luxury followed by supply poverty is a questionable lifestyle.
Leave money for meds and your eventual travel setup. The property doesn't need your entire life savings as a welcome gift.

sections.title: Getting your happy up
facts: Ecstasy doubles current happiness but has overdose risk; surplus happiness has a quarter-hour reset.
tips: Have the full sequence ready before using pricey happy boosters. Browsing the market while the timer runs is a high-budget thriller.
Go cheaper if an overdose or missed reset would wreck the plan. Training should not require a financial recovery arc.

sections.title: The Lists of Levelling Targets
facts: Target catalogues are references, not guarantees of unchanged stats or availability.
tips: Use the Baldr and Community filters, then check recent observations and your own results. A good list is a starting point, not a promise.
Look at the verification date. Ten days inactive once doesn't mean retired forever.

sections.title: Attacking the Levelling Targets
facts: A normal attack costs 25 energy and has a 25-turn, five-minute limit.
tips: If the target keeps winning, stop donating energy to the cause. Check accuracy, damage, life and gear, then train or switch targets.
For levelling, deliberately pick Leave after the win. The cash option is tempting, but that's a different mission.

level15.summary: Your route to travel access: affordable prep, fights you can win and fewer unnecessary hospital tours.
corrections: The archived equipment prices and 500-stat suggestion are examples, not current prices or a guaranteed combat threshold.
checklist: Equip sensible gear and sort your medical supplies.
Try a suitable target and note what happened.
Choose Leave for experience and take the available upgrades while chasing level 15.

extras.title: When a target stops being profitable
facts: Battle outcome depends on more than displayed level; no fixed beginner stat total guarantees a win.
tips: After repeat failures, inspect turns, damage, accuracy and recovery costs. More determination isn't a substitute for a better matchup.
A respected list can still contain a bad target for you today. Close the tab with dignity and find another one.

sections.title: Prerequisites
facts: Travel inventory and baggage rules changed in June 2026.
tips: Check method, capacity, supplies and restrictions on the actual travel screen. Your passport doesn't include immunity to old advice.
Price the whole round trip before departing. Abroad is a poor place to discover that the margin never existed.

sections.title: Renting Island
facts: Rented vault access is unavailable even if the property listing includes a vault upgrade.
tips: Confirm the airstrip and budget staff upkeep separately. The pilot doesn't accept spectacular ocean views as payment.
Compare a suitable lease before buying an island for one benefit. Start with the maths, then admire the swimming pool.

sections.title: Hiring a Pilot
facts: An airstrip and pilot give access to the corresponding travel method; an airstrip alone is not enough.
tips: Make sure the pilot is hired and the intended travel method is selected. Owning a runway doesn't make you an airline.
Include the recurring staff and property bill in your route maths. Those costs didn't disappear just because they're less exciting.

sections.title: Why you should only run flowers/plushies at start
facts: Flowers and plushies have museum-set demand; newer contraband has different pricing and risk.
tips: Treat flowers and plushies as an easy place to start, not a sacred oath against every other item.
Test demand and after-cost margin with a small load. Your first shipment doesn't need to be a dramatic financial statement.

sections.title: Flower/Plushie Running
facts: Default baggage is 10; the airstrip/WLT/business base is 15, before applicable bonuses.
tips: Use real capacity, both flights, today's buy price and after-fee resale proceeds. The calculator prefers numbers to vibes.
Pick a fallback item and a maximum wait. An empty shop is not obliged to respect your timetable.

after15.summary: Passport ready? Let's make the trip worthwhile instead of importing a suitcase full of questionable decisions.
corrections: The 2026 revision increased standard capacity and reduced suitcase bonuses; the archived +4 large-suitcase advice is outdated.
Black-market pricing is variable; a saved screenshot is not a current quote.
checklist: Check travel method, capacity and the ongoing housing bill.
Check stock and pick a backup item before heading out.
Compare net cash per round-trip hour, then deal with the sale proceeds promptly.

extras.title: Foreign shop pricing and inventory
facts: Contraband Importation introduced separate General Store, Arms Dealer and Black Market shops; drugs and contraband have variable prices.
tips: Saved shop prices are observations, not a pinky promise. Check the price again before buying.
Check the travel inventory and leave the space your plan needs. An old capacity screenshot cannot carry the extra item for you.

tables.title: Current baggage reference
rows: Airstrip plus pilot / WLT / Business Class base
These alternative bases do not add together.
Only the largest applicable suitcase counts.
Use your own active faction perks.
Do not assume a flower bonus applies to all goods.

sections.title: NPO - Valour
facts: Its recruitment thread describes Valour as an entry-level branch, but current acceptance and perks must be confirmed.
tips: Ask which requirements have exceptions below level 15. A recruitment table is the start of the conversation, not the bouncer's final verdict.
Read the current first post and ask admissions before planning around a perk. Old screenshots don't issue membership cards.

sections.title: WTF Family
facts: The imported family description is historical; a family name does not verify the policies of each branch.
tips: Ask which exact faction ID fits your goals. A family name can cover several very different daily routines.
Compare war schedules, vault access and membership rules branch by branch. Same surname, different house rules.

sections.title: WTF
facts: Current recruitment availability and perks were not independently verified for this historical entry.
tips: Confirm the faction ID with a current profile or recruiter. Similar names are a poor substitute for checking.
Get today's expectations and payout terms. An archived welcome speech cannot promise you this week's perks.

sections.title: WTF Medical
facts: The old guide describes a medical branch; present revive benefits and recruitment status are unverified.
tips: Ask the current revive-energy cost and whether you need Brain Surgeon before joining. Check the job description before collecting the imaginary white coat.
Check contracts, training support and payment for failed attempts. A failed revive shouldn't also come with surprise accounting.

sections.title: WTF Healers
facts: The historical healer listing is not a current offer of membership or a verified perk guarantee.
tips: Compare their revive-training support with your own job progress. A promising role still needs a realistic route into it.
Ask about attendance and contract payouts. Generous needs a definition before you spend the energy.

sections.title: Toxic Spawn
facts: A community beginner-faction list references Toxic Spawn; this does not verify a present vacancy.
tips: Check the current profile, recruiter and requirements. An old beginner list is a lead, not a reserved seat.
Ask how moving to another branch works and what it costs or requires. Read the stairs before climbing the ladder.

sections.title: New Sith Order
facts: The recruitment thread distinguishes a war-focused family branch; historic beginner suitability is not assured.
tips: Ask which branch suits your stats and schedule. The Force is useful, but so is reading the recruitment requirements.
Check war duties and supply policies against your budget. A dramatic faction name shouldn't be the entire business case.

sections.title: TORNado
facts: A faction recruitment thread exists, but an old thread title cannot establish current vacancies or perks.
tips: Check the first post and the recruiter's latest reply date. An old OPEN title may have taken a very long lunch.
Get current training, supply and withdrawal terms before depositing much money. Forecast first, faction-themed weather jokes later.

sections.title: We Are Rising
facts: No sufficiently current recruitment offer was verified for this archived name and ID.
tips: Use the numeric ID from the source so a rename or lookalike doesn't send you to the wrong doorstep.
Confirm today's leadership and recruitment rules in Torn. The old directory can't speak for whoever runs things now.

sections.title: NNGO Deja 2
facts: Current recruitment and benefits were not verified for this historical directory entry.
tips: Check for a rename, reorganisation or a changed purpose. Factions can have character development too.
Compare current perks and duties before calling it a beginner option. Historic friendliness is not a live vacancy.

factions-new-players.summary: Find your people, not just a nice banner and an exciting list of possibly ancient perks.
corrections: Named entries are historical leads. Present recruitment, ownership, requirements and perks are not guaranteed.
checklist: Compare active perks with the duties you'll actually be expected to do.
Read current recruitment info and confirm the faction ID.
Get supplies, payouts and vault withdrawals explained before you commit.

extras.title: Current faction selection checklist
facts: Faction resources, upgrades and membership terms differ; a historical directory is not a live offer.
tips: Ask about active perks, war frequency, supplies, payout deductions and withdrawals. Get the practical answers before falling in love with the banner.
Pick a faction you can actually keep up with. An unsustainable perk package is just a fancy source of stress.

sections.title: Mugging
facts: Mugging takes a variable proportion of exposed cash and can be modified by perks.
tips: Know where the payment is going before it lands. A wallet full of sale proceeds can become someone else's exciting afternoon.
Don't assume a hospital plan, high net worth or a tiny earlier mug makes the next receipt safe. Different money, different situation.

sections.title: Mug Protection
facts: Post-mug protected cash decays over 12 hours; moving protected funds can reduce that protection.
tips: Don't shuffle protected cash around assuming the original protection survives intact. Moving money has consequences beyond tidying the numbers.
Treat protection as damage limitation, not a VIP invitation to leave the next payment sitting out.

sections.title: Cash Storage
facts: Storage choices differ in access, lockup, volatility and counterparty risk.
tips: Split emergency spending from investments and deadline money. Not every dollar needs the same bedtime and wake-up call.
Know how you'll get funds back before depositing or buying anything. Future you might need cash, not an exciting explanation.

sections.title: Piggy Bank
facts: The beginner piggy bank is a one-time opportunity; withdrawing destroys it and puts the balance in hand.
tips: Check George's store early. The pig is a limited opportunity, not a permanent branch of your local bank.
Choose the next destination before smashing it. The pig disappears; the wallet exposure makes a fresh entrance.

sections.title: Ghost Trades
facts: An unfinished trade can be cancelled; completed acceptance transfers its contents.
tips: Don't mistake temporary holding for an interest account or a forever vault. The ghost bit doesn't make it magical.
Use someone you trust and agree clearly that the holding trade must stay unfinished. Accidental completion is a very literal disappearing act.

sections.title: How to set a ghost trade?
facts: The initiating player has the final acceptance step in direct trading.
tips: Check the recipient ID and purpose, leave the trade unfinished and watch its state. Small details, annoyingly large consequences.
Set a reminder to review it. Your emergency funds shouldn't depend on a conversation everyone forgot about.

sections.title: City Bank
facts: Time deposits offer several durations with changing APR; matured funds can remain in the bank until withdrawn.
tips: Compare today's return with the date you'll need the money. The biggest interest number isn't automatically the most useful offer.
Keep a reserve outside the locked deposit. The bank does not unlock early because you suddenly remembered an expense.

sections.title: Cayman Island
facts: Offshore interest uses the month's lowest qualifying balance, and access requires being abroad.
tips: Count the travel and time cost as well as the interest. Offshore does not automatically mean clever.
Don't expect a late-month deposit to earn a whole month's interest. The calendar has noticed when you arrived.

sections.title: Stocks
facts: Stock sales have a 0.1% fee and trading is restricted in hospital, jail and transit.
tips: Stocks can fall and may be inaccessible when you need them. That's a rather important footnote for a supposed cash vault.
Don't make an urgent bill depend on an instant stock sale. Your hospital timer and the market may have other ideas.

sections.title: Points
facts: Points are a separate currency and must normally be exchanged through their own market.
tips: Check the buy/sell spread before parking money in points. A round trip through the market can have a toll booth.
Keep refill points apart from resale stock. Otherwise your training budget may wander off wearing an investment label.

sections.title: Items
facts: Different items have different markets, restrictions and liquidity.
tips: Only store value in items you know how to price and sell. A cupboard full of mystery purchases is not diversification.
Estimate what you can actually receive after costs. Your inventory's impressive estimated value doesn't pay the next bill by itself.

sections.title: Property Vaults
facts: A tenant cannot access a rented property's vault.
tips: Check ownership, access and capacity before making plans. A vault on a rental listing can look wonderfully useful right up until you try to open it.
Don't pay extra rent for vault access you won't get. That's a very decorative expense.

sections.title: Faction Vault
facts: Faction resources are controlled by members with the relevant permissions.
tips: Ask who handles withdrawals and when they're around. Online eventually is less helpful than an actual policy.
Keep your own deposit record and don't stash money you may urgently need. Waiting for an officer is not an instant-access account.

sections.title: Company Vaults
facts: A company vault is part of a player-run business, not your personal bank.
tips: Keep business and personal cash separate in your notes. One big number can hide several very different obligations.
Think about director access, sale terms and liabilities before using the company as storage. It's a business, not a giant piggy bank.

sections.title: Winning the lottery / Slots / Big Money Quick Storage
facts: Some large receipts use cashier's checks while other payouts can create immediate wallet exposure.
tips: Check exactly how the payout arrives before claiming. Big money deserves a plan longer than ooh, shiny.
Handle the cash exposure before announcing the win. The city has an enthusiastic audience for that sort of news.

sections.title: Slots Win
facts: Casino activity can create large gains or losses; it is not a reliable savings method.
tips: After a strange and wonderful win, pause and protect it. The next spin does not owe you a sequel.
Don't assume slots use the same claim process as a lottery cheque. Check the actual payout rather than the family resemblance.

sections.title: Lottery Win
facts: Lottery winnings are cashier's checks that automatically credit after 24 hours if not collected.
tips: Set a reminder before automatic credit and plan the destination. A deadline can move the cash even when you've gone to bed.
Check the bank record yourself. An unexpected you won message isn't proof of anything except an unexpected message.

sections.title: Investing your winnings
facts: Bank rates vary and stock prices can fall; a quoted return is not a guarantee.
tips: Set aside training, housing and emergency money first. Let your future self keep a few functioning plans.
Compare the next benefit block's own cost and yield before buying several. A shopping spree doesn't become analysis because the items pay dividends.

money-storage.summary: Give your cash a sensible home. Your wallet would love fewer surprise visitors.
corrections: A rented property does not provide vault access.
Stocks can lose value and are unavailable in some game states; they are not an instant guaranteed vault.
Mug protection can change when protected cash is moved.
checklist: Choose the storage destination before a big payment lands.
Keep an operating float for expenses you can already see coming.
Set reminders for deposits, temporary holdings and automatic cheque credits.

extras.title: A plan for a predictable cash receipt
facts: Different payout mechanisms can put money in hand immediately or after a claim deadline.
tips: Pick the claim time, destination and access route before the money arrives. Storage first, casual browsing afterwards.
Make the move manually and check the balance in Torn. A helper notification is not the final bank statement.

sections.title: For Newbies
facts: Early earning methods consume different combinations of time, energy and capital.
tips: Choose an earner that funds your next unlock without eating all your growth resources. The hustle should help the account, not hold it hostage.
Log net cash and time for a week. Your results are allowed to disagree with a very confident forum post.

sections.title: Selling Losses/Slutting
facts: Paid losses use attack energy that could otherwise support levelling or gym training.
tips: Agree quantity, weapons, proof and payment timing before the first attack. Losing the fight is the service; losing the agreement is optional.
Subtract recovery costs and compare the lost progression. Try a small batch with a new buyer before committing your whole energy bar.

sections.title: City Shops
facts: Shop purchase cost and player resale value are separate prices.
tips: Check stock and today's demand before buying. Historic beer margins don't travel forward in time with the guide.
Count fees and unsold items. Bought cheaply and actually made money are two different milestones.

sections.title: Odd Jobs
facts: Player services rely on a specific agreement rather than a built-in salary guarantee.
tips: Agree one clear deliverable, price, deadline and acceptance standard. Something useful for a fair amount is how disputes get a running start.
Stay within Torn's rules: no account access and no real-money exchanges. A side hustle doesn't need a ban as a bonus feature.

sections.title: Advertising
facts: Trade and Global have different permitted uses; old spam-based advice is unsuitable.
tips: Use the right channel and track genuine replies or sales. Counting messages mostly tells you how busy your fingers were.
Agree placement and duration before paying someone to advertise. Exposure is not a sufficiently detailed invoice.

sections.title: Company Employee Finding
facts: Companies need staff suited to their positions and operating model.
tips: Get the director's stat, activity and retention requirements first. Recruiting the wrong fit is an impressively busy way to achieve nothing.
Agree what earns the fee and when. You're finding candidates, not appointing yourself the director's hiring department.

sections.title: Community Events
facts: Event eligibility and rewards depend on each organiser's published conditions.
tips: Enter when the likely fun or reward justifies the cost. A colourful prize list is allowed to remain someone else's adventure.
Save the entry proof and check the payout process. Winners shouldn't need to win a second contest to collect.

sections.title: Fun & Forum / Discord Servers
facts: Off-site communities do not replace Torn's game rules or account-security controls.
tips: Verify invitations through a known profile or thread. Random direct messages have an excellent imagination.
Don't pay a verification fee or hand over keys for a surprise prize. Free stuff shouldn't need your account's plumbing.

sections.title: City Map
facts: City finds can spawn after daily activity; more clicking does not produce more spawns.
tips: Collect finds in a short routine and price unusual items before selling. Your accidental treasure deserves a quick check.
Don't budget around rare windfalls. Found a fortune is a pleasant event, not a dependable salary.

sections.title: GFX Design
facts: Creative work for Torn assets still needs to respect the game's trading rules.
tips: Agree dimensions, format, revisions, delivery and usage rights first. Make it pop is not a complete creative brief.
Use a small paid milestone and keep previews or receipts. Unlimited revisions is a dangerous phrase in any universe.

sections.title: Responsible gambling
facts: Gambling outcomes are uncertain; token availability does not create a positive-return income method.
tips: Keep gambling winnings out of the money needed for rent, training and supplies. Those bills need a steadier plan.
Set an affordable entertainment limit. If you're chasing a loss, stop rather than feeding progression money into the attempt.

sections.title: Companies
facts: Directors manage staff, stock and advertising; gross revenue is not net business profit.
tips: Ask for operating records and liabilities before buying. A good-looking company page is not an audit.
Price a bad week of wages, ads and inventory. If that scenario wrecks the budget, the business is already giving you useful feedback.

sections.title: City Bank
facts: The normal investment ceiling is $2 billion; a qualifying Oil Rig benefit can raise it.
tips: Use the current offer and keep known expenses liquid. Your next investment should match your actual calendar.
Don't pool or borrow money because an old rate looked amazing. A historic bargain cannot cover a current obligation.

sections.title: Intermediate
facts: Service and faction income depend on skill, opportunities, terms and actual participation.
tips: Pick a repeatable method that fits your schedule. Being a part-time version of every veteran at once sounds exhausting.
Track net income alongside energy and availability. An excellent earner you can't actually do is mostly a nice story.

sections.title: Reviving
facts: Reviving unlocks through Brain Surgeon; attempts consume energy even when they fail.
tips: Agree whether pay is per attempt or per success before starting. Better to settle the definition while everyone is still calm.
Use displayed chance and energy cost to estimate expected pay per energy. A cheerful quoted rate isn't the whole calculation.

sections.title: Flower/Plushie Running
facts: Foreign stock availability and local resale demand can change between departures.
tips: Rank routes after costs and count both flights, waiting and selling time. Profit per hour likes the complete clock.
Compare buyers and keep a backup route. Yesterday's winner doesn't have a permanent seat at the top of the spreadsheet.

sections.title: Stocks Benefit Blocks
facts: Passive benefits have a holding period; active dividends need claiming before another cycle progresses.
tips: Set collection reminders and price the next increment separately. Passive income can still require you to press a button.
Value item rewards at a realistic after-fee sale price. Imaginary full-price buyers are wonderfully generous and rarely available.

sections.title: Bounties
facts: Claiming a bounty requires a qualifying hospitalisation; a high bounty does not imply an easy target.
tips: Check strength and status before spending energy or recovery items. The reward number isn't an assessment of your chances.
Compare expected net pay with failed attempts and missed training. A bounty can pay someone well without that someone being you.

sections.title: Ranked Warring
facts: Weekly ranked-war templates were introduced in November 2026; enlistment shows the applicable rules.
tips: Read this week's template before planning. Last week's score target may have left the building.
Agree payout rules and deductions before the war, then keep the report. Post-war arithmetic is more peaceful with fewer surprises.

sections.title: Building Flower/Plushie Sets
facts: The History bachelor unlocks museum exchanges; complete flower or plushie sets exchange for points.
tips: Price the complete set, including the awkward item, against current point proceeds. One missing plushie can have expensive opinions.
Include fees, tied-up cash and assembly time. Completing a set is satisfying; making a profit is a separate achievement.

sections.title: Events/Competitions
facts: Special bonuses have event-specific start and end conditions.
tips: Check your own event slot before shopping or scheduling big actions. Other people's calendars don't get to set yours.
Budget for the ordinary result. A rare prize is a lovely bonus, not next week's guaranteed rent.

sections.title: Mugging
facts: Mug results are variable and affected by protection and perks.
tips: Don't treat a visible sale or old net-worth number as a guaranteed wallet balance. The money may already have better accommodation.
Count failed attacks, retaliation and lost training time. The gross mug is only the headline, not the whole article.

sections.title: Advanced
facts: Trading and businesses introduce more capital and liquidity risk than a simple service sale.
tips: Keep a ledger of cost basis, fees, inventory and tied-up cash. Your memory is not a regulated accounting system.
Scale once you can explain both the profit and the failure case. Trust me, it works is not a stress test.

sections.title: Trading
facts: Item-market sales carry fees; direct trades and bazaars have different processes and exposure.
tips: Subtract fees, slow stock, price movement and your own time. The spread isn't all yours just because it looks tempting.
Test an unfamiliar item with a small purchase first. Tuition is cheaper when the lesson is not bought in bulk.

sections.title: Stocks
facts: Share-price gains are distinct from dividend benefits and neither guarantees profit.
tips: Track realised proceeds after the sale fee and keep near-term bill money out of speculation. Paper gains are very bad at paying invoices.
Don't call a guessed pattern a reliable signal. A chart can make a convincing face without predicting anything.

sections.title: Mercenaries
facts: Outside combat services depend on game restrictions and a buyer's agreed qualifying conditions.
tips: Define eligible targets, finish result, proof, pay and exclusions before taking the work. Paid to fight shouldn't become unpaid to argue.
Reconcile against reports. A visible hit doesn't automatically satisfy whatever the buyer agreed to count.

money-making.summary: Making money is good. Making money after counting the costs is even better.
corrections: Old sale-price and hourly-income examples are not live earning guarantees.
The ordinary item-market sales fee is 5%; a route or trade must account for its actual selling channel.
Ranked-war templates now make checking the current enlistment rules important.
checklist: Pick a repeatable earner and count every relevant cost.
Leave room for training, progression and near-term bills.
Scale after completed results support the margin, not just because the idea sounds excellent.

extras.title: Marginal return versus total return
facts: An additional investment can have a different cost and yield from the first one.
tips: Compare the next upgrade on its extra cost alone. Your cheap first purchase shouldn't be doing all the PR for the expensive next one.
Use realistic sale prices and a bad-case scenario. The spreadsheet needs at least one row where things don't go perfectly.

tables.title: Net return worksheet (editorial calculation)
rows: Sale proceeds after fees − purchase cost
Use the fee of the actual selling channel.
Quantity × unit margin − other trip costs
Include paid travel and allocated recurring costs.
Include both flights, waiting and selling time.
Illustrative example, not a price quote
Expected net pay ÷ total energy spent
Include unsuccessful attempts and unpaid work.

sections.title: A Criminal Primer
facts: The player-authored Criminal Primer includes an October 2026 Arson update; it remains community guidance.
tips: Use the crime-specific notes here alongside the current interface and linked wiki. Bring the right rulebook to the right minigame.
Keep documented mechanics separate from players' best-method estimates. Very confident is not a probability calculation.

extras.title: Search for Cash
facts: All six searches cost two nerve. Beach and cemetery require unlock items; the fountain needs skill 75.
tips: Check each location's current conditions. There isn't one forever-best search button hiding behind the interface.
Decide whether you're chasing cash or uniques, then check unlock items. Aimless clicking is a hobby, not a plan.

extras.title: Bootlegging
facts: Copying, selling and an online store are separate activities. The store needs skill 50, the named web-design course and a computer.
tips: Count blank DVDs and selling time. A giant pile of copied stock isn't profit until it actually sells.
Check production and existing stock before copying more. Your pretend DVD empire probably doesn't need another unsold mountain.

extras.title: Graffiti
facts: Area reputation changes independently and decays; the Paint Mask is its enhancer. Some areas require a crew unlock.
tips: Build reputation somewhere deliberately instead of scattering every early attempt across town. Even fictional vandalism benefits from a plan.
Watch paint supplies and decide whether you're here for rep or cash. The wall has room; your nerve budget may not.

extras.title: Shoplifting
facts: Each shop has its own notoriety and security state. Notoriety falls over time; four nerve is used per attempt.
tips: Watch local notoriety and rotate or pause when it makes sense. The shop can remember you even when you'd prefer it didn't.
Disabled cameras aren't a guarantee. Leave room in the budget for failures and lost supplies instead of trusting your inner action hero.

extras.title: Pickpocketing
facts: Targets vary by type, body and current distraction; availability does not mean suitability for your skill.
tips: Choose manageable targets and watch expiry timers. Every new row isn't a personal invitation.
Log failures by target type. Your own results are a better coach than a stranger promising totally safe money.

extras.title: Card Skimming
facts: Installation uses a card skimmer and spy camera; details become usable on recovery, and devices can be lost.
tips: Longer placement means a return-versus-loss-risk choice. More time is not automatically more clever.
Keep a placement log and count replacement gear. A vanished device has a very direct opinion about your profit margin.

extras.title: Burglary
facts: Scout, case and burglarize are distinct actions. Casing confidence fades; a target's recommended item unlocks its unique reward.
tips: Leave enough nerve to finish the target you chose. Collecting locations you'll never use is basically property-window shopping.
Check the recommended item and current confidence before the final step. Focused scouting costs more, so make the choice on purpose.

extras.title: Hustling
facts: Audience interest, suspicion and each game's technique affect play. Shill and pickpocket helpers unlock at higher skill.
tips: Build a game deliberately and watch the audience. Hammering Win isn't the entire art of fictional confidence tricks.
Include intentional losses and helper collections in the maths. Your session summary shouldn't develop selective amnesia.

extras.title: Disposal
facts: Jobs arrive daily and can only be attempted once. Method choice and required consumables vary by job.
tips: Read the job and compare methods. The expensive button is not automatically the smart button.
Check supplies and note what worked. Your next job deserves better than another round of enthusiastic guessing.

extras.title: Cracking
facts: This in-game minigame requires Introduction to Computing and a computer. Wrong character guesses can lock further guesses.
tips: Keep this entirely inside Torn's minigame. Real accounts and other people's passwords are not part of the assignment.
Price rig upgrades against jobs your skill can use. Don't burn guesses just because the empty character box looks inviting.

extras.title: Forgery
facts: Projects have multiple five-nerve steps, mixed reusable and consumed tools, and possible progress loss.
tips: Price the full finished item before starting a batch. Half a project and a cupboard of supplies aren't a completed payday.
Stagger timed steps around normal logins. A hundred unfinished projects is an ambitious way to organise a queue.

extras.title: Scamming
facts: The fictional crime uses an in-game address pool, responses and a reward-zone minigame.
tips: Use only the fictional Torn activity. Never gather real email addresses or message real people for this guide.
Watch the cursor and zones, and budget the whole conversation. The final payout screenshot conveniently forgets all the earlier nerve.

extras.title: Arson
facts: The in-game scenario uses different fire behaviour, client requirements and unlockable tools; Collect has its own final step.
tips: Keep this strictly in Torn's game interface and read the fictional job requirements. The real world is not DLC.
Check consumable costs and final conditions before doing more actions. A dramatic animation doesn't mean the job is ready to collect.

extras.title: Crime progression without false guarantees
facts: Success, failure and critical failure affect progression differently; higher happiness helps progression rather than known success chance.
tips: Track cash, skill and uniques separately. The best cash route and the fastest progression route needn't be best friends.
Use current indicators and budget for losses. Zero risk needs evidence, not just extra capital letters.

crimes2.summary: Torn's crime menu has more moving parts than click button, receive fortune. Here's the useful version.
corrections: Do not use the archived claim that the system has only twelve crimes as a current count.
Crime experience, individual crime skill, progression bonuses and hidden success formulas are different concepts.
checklist: Choose your target: cash, progression or unique outcomes.
Check skill, tools, consumables and current conditions.
Log net proceeds and failures. A bigger nerve price tag doesn't automatically mean a better deal.

sections.title: Step 1: Visit the traders profile
facts: A direct trade can start from a player's profile or the inventory Trades interface.
tips: Check the numeric ID. A familiar-looking avatar is not an identity document.
Agree price and quantity in writing with a new trader. Avoid starting the deal with a collaborative guessing game.

sections.title: Step 2: Click on the trade icon
facts: The initiating party controls final completion after the other party accepts.
tips: Make sure you're opening a trade, not sending items or money. Those buttons lead to very different afternoons.
Keep the agreed quote visible while reviewing. Your memory doesn't need to carry the whole transaction.

sections.title: Step 3: Fill Description on new trade panel
facts: A description labels the trade; it does not replace checking its actual contents.
tips: Use item, quantity and price basis in the description. Mystery trade is a title for a bad story, not a useful label.
Make simultaneous trades easy to tell apart. Two identical vague descriptions are asking your future self to improvise.

sections.title: Step 4: Use the Plus Buttons to add Items/Money
facts: Money and ordinary items are tradeable; points and shares are not normal direct-trade contents.
tips: Check the quantity and exact variant before adding the whole stack. Similar names can have impressively different prices.
Do your own arithmetic on the cash total. Someone else's screenshot doesn't get the final vote.

sections.title: Step 5: Wait for the trader to add money
facts: The other party's acceptance locks the proposed contents against further changes.
tips: Look for the actual locked trade state. Added in chat is a sentence, not a payment record.
If the expected cash or item isn't there, stop. Urgency is not a replacement currency.

sections.title: Step 6: Trader has accepted, now its your turn
facts: Final acceptance includes a reconfirmation delay; cancellation remains possible before completion.
tips: Use the last check for both sides, recipient and exact amount. This is a good time to be gloriously boring.
Know where a large cash receipt will go before accepting. Celebrate after the money has suitable accommodation.

how-to-set-trade.summary: Six steps to a sensible trade. Let's keep the drama out of the final confirmation.
corrections: A description or chat promise does not prove payment has been added.
Points and shares cannot be placed into an ordinary direct trade.
checklist: Agree the quote and check who you're actually trading with.
Review the contents of the real locked trade.
Check the exact amount one last time and plan where any incoming cash goes.

extras.title: If a transaction changes or feels wrong
facts: A direct trade can be cancelled before final completion.
tips: If price, item or recipient changes, stop and inspect the actual trade again. The original agreement didn't automatically approve a plot twist.
Don't complete under pressure. A clean restart is cheaper than an impressively fast mistake.

sections.title: How Often should I run through pages
facts: Egg spawns are activity-independent; unfound eggs persist and can roll over into the next event.
tips: Browse manually at sensible intervals. Refreshing like a frantic chicken doesn't make the egg supply more generous.
Check the current calendar window. An Easter guide being available in November is not a surprise event announcement.

sections.title: How do I use scripts on Mobile Devices
facts: Scripts must follow Torn's current scripting rules; software must not auto-request hidden game pages or click rewards.
tips: Read the source and permissions before installing a script, and check it fits today's Torn rules. Popular is not a permission setting.
An old recommendation isn't a security review. Skip unfamiliar extensions that ask for more access than makes sense.

sections.title: Eggs Usage Guide
facts: Collected eggs are non-tradeable inventory items; using one adds six hours of booster cooldown.
tips: Have a goal and enough cooldown room before eating the egg. This is resource planning, with chocolate.
Percentage rewards may help more later. Compare what you can use now with what waiting might gain, rather than eating the shiny thing on sight.

easter.summary: Find eggs, enjoy chocolate-flavoured resource planning and leave the refresh-button workout behind.
corrections: Refreshing does not increase the activity-independent spawn rate.
Collected eggs are inventory items, not immediate rewards that must be used when found.
This is a seasonal reference, not a statement that Easter is active today.
checklist: Check the calendar and your own event slot.
Browse manually and stick to permitted tools.
Use eggs when their rewards and cooldown cost fit your plan.

extras.title: Booster planning around an egg
facts: An egg uses six hours of booster cooldown; surplus happy still has its normal timing constraint.
tips: Leave cooldown space and prepare the activity first. The reward works better with a plan than with an immediate shopping trip.
Don't spend resources chasing guaranteed colours or secret spawn schedules. Eggs are mysterious enough without buying somebody's conspiracy theory.

Do your chosen crimes and supplies support it?
Will you train before the next happy reset?
Is a planned combat window worth using it?
Is enough addiction present to justify using it?
Would a larger balance make waiting worthwhile?
Compare using now with delaying for larger stats.
